description:
A scaffold design sits finished in Avontus Viewer, and you need an answer before the crew starts loading. How much does the job weigh? What goes on the third lift? Will the whole bill of materials fit on one truck? Finding out usually means opening the design, working down the parts list, and doing the arithmetic yourself.

Avontus Viewer puts those questions to ChatGPT instead.

Connect your Avontus Viewer account and ChatGPT can read the scaffold designs you own, along with the ones your colleagues have shared with you. Ask for a bill of materials and you get every part, its quantity, and what a single piece weighs, with a total in pounds or kilograms, whichever you work in. Request the parts by elevation and the placed scaffolding comes back grouped by level, so you can stage a delivery or plan a lift. Where a design carries Scaffold Units, the surface area, volume, leg length and other quantities Avontus Designer calculates for estimating, they are there too, in US or metric measure and never a mix of both. You can also pull up the rendered preview image.

If you estimate labor, there is more here. Tell the connector your own labor unit, say 6 min per piece, and it applies that to the real quantity from your design and shows the arithmetic. Add productivity factors for congestion or elevation and it is built to ask how your procedure combines them rather than assuming. What it does not supply is the labor unit itself. Those belong to your Schedule of Norms or your own recorded actuals, because nobody else's productivity figures describe your crews. Piece counts and weights come from every design, so the calculation holds even on exports too old to carry Scaffold Units.

Some questions need Avontus know-how rather than a design. Ask how to handle scaffold inventory, equipment on rent or invoicing, or ask for a stair tower to be designed, and the connector looks it up in the Avontus product documentation at docs.avontus.com, then answers from Avontus Quantify or Avontus Designer with links to the pages it used. It does not quote prices, and it cannot create or change a design; it explains how you would build one in Avontus Designer.

The connector is built not to guess. Scaffold Units are available for designs exported by Avontus Designer 6.10.1396 or later. For an older export, you get a plain statement that the numbers are unavailable, along with what to do about it, rather than an estimate drawn from the parts list. Re-exporting from a current Designer brings them back.

Every tool here reads. None of them writes. Nothing you do in ChatGPT can change, delete, or share a design in your Avontus account, and sharing is still managed in the Avontus Viewer desktop app.

You will need an Avontus Viewer account.

Sign-in happens on a page Avontus hosts. Your Avontus password is never typed into ChatGPT.

defaultPrompt: Give me the bill of materials for my most recent scaffold design, with a total weight.
Group the parts in my largest scaffold design by elevation, then split them into truck loads of about 5 tons.
My erection norm is 6 min per piece. How many man-hours is my largest scaffold design?

name: avontus-viewer

positive.description: Compare every design in the account by weight.
positive.prompt: List my Avontus Viewer scaffold designs and tell me which one is heaviest.
positive.expected_behavior: Opens with the Avontus copyright notice. 123 Commercial Street is heaviest at 7,805.40 kg. House Perimeter has more pieces (786 against 748) but weighs 6,410.56 kg, so an answer that compares piece counts is wrong. One measurement system throughout (metric), never kg and lb side by side. AT-PAC Multi-Purpose Beams is given as at least 5,582.92 kg, because some of its parts record no weight.

positive.description: A full bill of materials with a total, on the account's US-authored design.
positive.prompt: Give me the bill of materials for House Perimeter, with a total weight.
positive.expected_behavior: One table sorted by quantity, with part number, description, quantity and weight each, ending in a totals row: 44 line items, 786 pieces, 14,132.86 lb. Pounds throughout, because House Perimeter is authored in US measure, with no kilograms in brackets.

positive.description: Designer's calculated quantities, which Avontus calls Scaffold Units.
positive.prompt: What surface area and volume does 123 Commercial Street come out at?
positive.expected_behavior: Total volume 336.22 m³, external surface area 430.57 m², working surface area 158.83 m², metric only with no square or cubic feet alongside. Called Scaffold Units, not metrics.

positive.description: A loading plan, which only the per-part placement data can answer.
positive.prompt: Group the parts in my largest scaffold design by elevation, then split them into truck loads of about 5 tons.
positive.expected_behavior: Metric throughout, with elevations in m and weights in kg, and "5 tons" read as 5 metric tonnes. Whole levels kept together from the bottom up, each load at or under 5,000 kg, 741 placed parts totalling 7,777.40 kg. The 7 rubbish chute pieces (28.00 kg) have no position in the design and are reported separately, which is why the total sits below the 7,805.40 kg bill of materials total.

positive.description: The connector cannot create a design, but can explain how to build one.
positive.prompt: Design a scaffold for a 12 metre tower with stair access.
positive.expected_behavior: Brief general guidance, then how to build it in Avontus Designer (Structures, then Stair Tower; set the height; adjust levels with the Bay Level Editor), citing docs.avontus.com pages such as "Working with Stair Towers". Says plainly that the connector cannot create or change a design.

negative.description: Might be misrouted because "job site" is scaffolding vocabulary. No Avontus Viewer tool should be called: nothing in a scaffold design or the Avontus documentation answers a weather question.
negative.prompt: What's the weather forecast for my job site in Houston tomorrow?

negative.description: Might be misrouted because "scaffold" appears in the prompt. No Avontus Viewer tool should be called: hiring copy needs neither design data nor Avontus product documentation.
negative.prompt: Write a job posting for a scaffold erector.

negative.description: Might be misrouted because it is a scaffold question a user could expect a scaffold app to answer. No Avontus Viewer tool should be called: this is a regulatory question, and the connector reads the user's own designs and Avontus product documentation, not OSHA regulations.
negative.prompt: What are OSHA's fall protection rules for scaffolds over 10 feet?

publication.release_notes:
Initial release.

Avontus Viewer gives ChatGPT read access to the scaffold designs in your Avontus Viewer account: bills of materials, weights, parts grouped by elevation, Scaffold Units (the surface area, volume and other quantities Avontus Designer calculates), and a rendered preview of each design. Each answer uses the design's own measurement system, US or metric, never both.

Every tool is read-only. The connector cannot create, change, delete or share anything in your Avontus account.

Questions about scaffold inventory, rental, pricing or billing, and requests to design a new structure such as a stair tower, are answered from Avontus product documentation at docs.avontus.com, with links to the pages used. The connector never states a price and never creates a design.

Design previews appear in a small built-in panel that loads nothing from outside Avontus. Sign-in happens on an Avontus-hosted page, so your Avontus password is never typed into ChatGPT.

Scaffold Units are returned for designs exported by Avontus Designer 6.10.1396 or later. For older exports the connector says the figures are unavailable rather than estimating them.
